video_metadata.working_title: MICHIGAN 1987 Cold Case Solved After 35 Years — Justice for Roxanne Wood
video_metadata.topic_one_sentence: Roxanne Leigh Wood, 30, was murdered in her Niles Township, Michigan kitchen in the early hours of 20 February 1987; her husband Terry, who found her, lived under suspicion for 35 years until genetic genealogy and a discarded cigarette identified Patrick Wayne Gilham, who pleaded no contest to second-degree murder in 2022.
video_metadata.primary_emotion_to_evoke: grief and the slow injustice of lifelong suspicion, resolved by science and persistence

events.significance: On parole at time of murder

events.what_happened: Roxanne and Terry meet at home after work, drive separate cars to dinner, then go to a bowling alley where Terry bowls in a league
Roxanne heads home about 45 minutes before Terry; Terry arrives shortly after 1 a.m. and finds her dead on the kitchen floor; calls police

No sign of forced entry; open kitchen drawer where the knife thought to be the weapon was kept; investigators say Terry was belligerent with first responders and asked for an attorney when brought in for questioning
DNA preserved but not enough evidence to charge anyone; prosecutors did not believe there was enough to charge Terry
WSBT 'Cold Case Files': MSP Det. Suarez calls Terry the main person of interest; Terry declines on camera, says 'I didn't murder Roxanne.'
Identifinders International begins examining the unknown DNA; WMU Cold Case Program students digitize ~3,500 pages

events.what_happened: Investigators collect a publicly discarded cigarette butt; lab reports match to crime-scene DNA (1 in 958.8 trillion)
MSP interviews Gilham; he denies going to Michigan except for work, having friends in Niles, knowing the Woods' street, or dating women in Niles
Gilham, 67, arrested at his home; charged with open murder and breaking and entering; held in St. Joseph County pending extradition
Gilham pleads no contest to second-degree murder; deal includes minimum 23 years; offered with family input including Terry

the_moment.what_is_happening: Terry Wood comes home about 45 minutes after Roxanne and finds her dead on the kitchen floor
the_moment.what_makes_it_shocking: The man who found her would be suspected for 35 years
the_moment.ironic_twist: The killer lived about 10 miles away in South Bend, on parole, and was never on the list

cold_open_material.central_mystery_question: Who killed Roxanne Wood in those 45 minutes, and what did 35 years of suspicion cost the man who found her

the_method.technique_name: Investigative genetic genealogy from trace DNA, confirmed by a discarded cigarette butt
step_by_step_explanation: Crime-scene DNA preserved since 1987 [1] CBS News / 48 Hours: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/roxanne-wood-murder-timeline-48-hours/

Identifinders generates a genetic profile from very little DNA (about 3 percent of normal) [3] CBS News / 48 Hours: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/roxanne-wood-murder-patrick-gilham-genetic-genealogist-helps-solve-case-that-had-a-gnats-eyebrow-of-dna/

Profile compared with relatives in public genealogy databases [2] CBS News / 48 Hours: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/roxanne-wood-murder-patrick-wayne-gilham-dna-detective-helped-solve-michigan-cold-case/

Vargas builds family tree in about four days, reaching three brothers [2] CBS News / 48 Hours: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/roxanne-wood-murder-patrick-wayne-gilham-dna-detective-helped-solve-michigan-cold-case/; [10] WOOD-TV 8: https://www.woodtv.com/news/michigan/woman-who-helped-solve-roxanne-wood-case-shares-story/

MSP surveillance; cigarette butt collected 3 June 2021 [5] Michigan State Police press release: https://content.govdelivery.com/attachments/MIMSP/2022/03/18/file_attachments/2108015/Gilham%20No%20Contest%20Plea%203-18-22.pdf; [7] Leader Publications (Niles Daily Star): https://www.leaderpub.com/2022/03/16/roxanne-wood-murder-police-report-details-interview-with-suspect-evidence/
Lab match 1 in 958.8 trillion [7] Leader Publications (Niles Daily Star): https://www.leaderpub.com/2022/03/16/roxanne-wood-murder-police-report-details-interview-with-suspect-evidence/
the_method.why_it_worked: Public genealogy databases contained relatives; the WMU digitized file let detectives check the name against 3,500 pages

technical_terms_to_explain.simple_explanation: hundreds of thousands of genetic letters compared with cousins, unlike the 13-20 markers of a police profile
defendant does not admit guilt but does not contest; court enters a conviction
Michigan charge letting the jury/court decide first or second degree

the_method.scale_of_operation: ~3,500 pages, several thousand student hours, ~10 months lab work, 4 days of genealogy, about 18 months MSP work

systemic_failure.institution_that_failed: 1987 investigation focus (tunnel vision on husband) and parole supervision context
systemic_failure.why_they_failed: No forced entry and Terry's behaviour and request for a lawyer were read as guilt; DNA technology insufficient
specific_incompetence_examples: Terry treated as main suspect even though witnesses placed him at the bowling alley [1] CBS News / 48 Hours: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/roxanne-wood-murder-timeline-48-hours/
Still described as main person of interest in 2013 [15] WSBT 22 (2013): https://wsbt.com/news/local/cold-case-files-police-have-a-suspect-in-26-year-old-murder-casebut-did-he-do-it
Gilham on parole for a sex-related offence months earlier [8] WOOD-TV 8: https://www.woodtv.com/news/michigan/suspect-in-1987-murder-on-parole-at-time-of-crime/
systemic_failure.ironic_details_about_the_failure: The DNA preserved in 1987 had always excluded the man people suspected (reported later).
